articles.title: Could weather force Yankees and Orioles into Friday doubleheader?
articles.summary: The Yankees are monitoring weather forecasts that could impact their final regular-season series with the Orioles at Yankee Stadium.
articles.body:
NEW YORK − The Yankees' final series of the regular season could be disrupted by the weather forecast.

The Yankees host the Baltimore Orioles this weekend in the Bronx, but there are discussions that the teams could play a doubleheader on Friday as the forecast is not looking good for both Saturday and Sunday.

Saturday's game, which is scheduled for 7:15 p.m., features a pregame ceremony in which CC Sabathia's number will be retired and his Monument Park plaque will be unveiled.

Sunday's game, the final game of the regular season, is scheduled for 3:20 p.m.

articles.title: How Kentucky keeps the momentum going and beats South Alabama
articles.summary: We lay out Kentucky's path to victory on Saturday against South Alabama and how the Wildcats finish the first month of the season with a 3-1 record.
articles.body:
The Kentucky Wildcats host South Alabama this weekend as they try to cap off the month of September by improving to a 3-1 record. The Jaguars are bringing in a run heavy offense to Kroger Field and a defense that has struggled to find success in 2026. Kentucky cannot start sluggish after a big win, they must come out hot and get to a fast start. Here is how Kentucky keeps the momentum going and improves to 3-1 on the season.

Kentucky's defense needs to slow down the rushing attack of the Jaguars and get off the field on third down. This is a game where the Wildcats defensive line should control the line of scrimmage. They have been good at limiting explosives in the run game, but they have given up almost four yards per carry. Kentucky has to dominate the line of scrimmage on Saturday and this defensive line has had a ton of different players flash through three weeks.

The defense may give up some points this weekend, but the offense has an opportunity to have an impressive showing against what might be the worst defense they will face all season. This is another matchup where the Kentucky offensive line can overwhelm the South Alabama defensive line. Teams have had great success through the air on the Jaguars, but they are also allowing five yards per carry on the ground. I think Kentucky can really lean on their run game and expect a big day from Jason Patterson as the staff will probably limit CJ Baxter to maintain his health.

In the passing game, Kenny Minchey can build off his exceptional performance from his first SEC road start. The staff put an emphasis to get DJ Miller going last week, and you got to wonder if they will do the same this week with Nic Anderson . Will Stein mentioned they shortened the play sheet so the offense could play fast and free against Texas A&M . I believe they open it up a bit more this weekend and try different looks to put on film.

Ohio played two quarterbacks against the Jaguars, and they combined to go 21-of-31 through the air for 234 yards and four touchdowns. Tulane's quarterback Kadin Semonza went 14-of-22 for 212 yards and a touchdown in their win over South Alabama. This passing attack from the Wildcats is the best they have seen to this point of the season, they could really struggle against this offensive scheme and all the playmakers Kentucky will feature. It would not surprise me if Minchey has another 300+ yard and 3+ touchdown performance like he had in week one against Youngstown State.

I don't think we see a sluggish, hangover start from the Wildcats on Saturday. This team is connected and Coach Stein has stated that after a big win is when he has to coach his team harder. Kentucky can be efficient in every aspect of the offense and the defense can get a real test of slowing down a spread offense that leans on the running game. I believe the Wildcats dominate this game in a lot of areas, but the talent mismatch on the line of scrimmage will be the main reason this one gets out of hand for South Alabama.

articles.title: Ohio State's Matt Patricia has interesting take on the 2026 defense
articles.summary: Ohio State defensive coordinator Matt Patricia discusses where this year's defense is in comparison to last year... and offers an interesting opinion.
articles.body:
There's been a lot of discussion surrounding the defense of Ohio State through non-conference play -- some good, some bad, and some ugly. In the eyes of defensive coordinator Matt Patricia , this group is actually ahead of where it was at this time last year.

"I always look at the markers of where we build, grow and add concepts to the defense, and I would say we are a little bit ahead of last year from a full concept standpoint because we had some carryover from last year," Patricia said . "Last year it was a little bit slower-paced with that -- our guys handle it a little better. But right now it's about working through the personnel and the roles."

It's not often you lose multiple first-round draft picks and are further ahead than with them, but it makes sense. Year one under Patricia took longer to establish the identity, scheme, and system. In year two, multiple players have returned who have that understanding.

The push for Patricia is working through rotations, increased depth, and personnel.

"Last year we had that one group that played a lot for us," Patricia said. "... This year we have more depth, so there are more bodies to put into those roles, so it's more by committee than it was last year at this point. The encouraging thing for us is we are able to play a lot of guys right now ... trying to learn what guys do well and put them in those roles as we go. Having that depth is really good for us early in the season."

Through three games, Ohio State is giving up 13.5 points per game -- compared to 5.3 points per game a season ago. One of the biggest areas for improvement has been pressure, with just three sacks on the season and 13 tackles for loss.

The big wake-up call was against Texas in the second week of the season, a lesson that showed where and how the Buckeyes ' defense needed adjusting.

"We've certainly been in some tough competition here early in the season, which is great because we need it ... finding out how guys handle those moments is key for us now, getting into Big Ten play ... still trying to learn what guys do well and find those roles and putting them in those roles as we go."

Patricia said that with so many players on and off the field, constant communication has been one of the challenges early in the year. But he's happy it's improving, and it's an area of the defense that will only continue to get better.

"I think going into the season you have those teams that you know are going to be a journey and you're going to learn and grow as the season goes, and sometimes those are some of the better ones you wind up with. You have to get into that pressure and the fire to have those moments where you learn, execute, and get better."

The next moment for the Buckeyes is this weekend, when they open Big Ten play as Illinois comes to town .

articles.title: Mets muster just four hits in 3-1 loss to Rangers
articles.summary: The Mets dropped the final game of their three-game set against the Rangers, 3-1, on Thursday afternoon.
articles.body:
The Mets dropped the final game of their three-game set against the Rangers , 3-1, on Thursday afternoon.

Rookie Carson Benge kicked off the scoring for the Mets early, cracking a single out to right field and sending Francisco Lindor , who doubled in the Mets' first at-bat of the afternoon, home for his 63rd RBI of the season. Overall, the rookie went 1-for-4, grounding out in the fourth, flying out in the seventh, and striking out swinging in the ninth.

Heading into the game, Benge led the team in runs (83), batting average (.275), OBP (.338) and SLG (.420). With one more home run in any of the final three games of the season, he would become the first Met with both 20 homers and 20 steals in his rookie season.

The Rangers quickly retaliated, taking a one-run lead in the bottom of the first. Leadoff Justin Foscue singled to left field to start before Josh Jung slammed the ball into the left field stands at 104 mph, sending himself and Foscue around the bases for the 2-1 edge.

After several deadlocked innings, Corey Seager added to the Rangers' lead with a fly ball out to right field to open the bottom of the sixth. With the win, the Rangers snapped a three-game losing streak.

In the 15th start of his rookie season, Zac Thornton nearly replicated his performance from his last start Sept. 18 , allowing two runs on four hits, walking just one batter, and striking out four across five innings. Jung was the only Rangers batter to make serious contact with a ball tossed by Thornton, accounting for two of the four hits, both of which left the bat at over 95mph (his second hit, a line-drive double in the bottom of the fourth, clocked 96.5mph).

Jeffrey Yan took over for the southpaw for just two-thirds of the sixth inning, allowing two hits and walking Jung before being replaced by Austin Warren , who struck out two across 1.1 innings. Jack Weisenburger closed the game for the Mets with one allowed hit, one walk, and one strikeout in his one inning.

Rangers starter Kumar Rocker posted a similar game, owning the mound for five innings. He allowed three hits, walked two, and struck out four. The Mets drafted Rocker in 2021 before ultimately deciding not to sign him due to concerns about the health of his right arm. He was then redrafted by the Rangers in 2022 and has been with the organization since.

Robert Gracia , Tyler Alexander , Chase Silseth , and Jordan Montgomery pitched one inning each to round out the game for Texas . Only Alexander allowed a hit, and Silseth struck out two. Montgomery struck out one. -- Much of the excitement for the Mets came in the field rather than at the plate. In the bottom of the second, Rangers left fielder Wyatt Langford took off from first in an attempt to steal second but was caught by Mets catcher Luis Torrens , who calmly caught Thornton's pitch and fired it down the field to Marcus Semien for the out. Later, when Jake Burger tried to steal third in the bottom of the sixth, Torrens quickly tossed the ball back to Semien to trap Burger between the bases. After Burger slipped on his way back to second, Semien tagged him out as he scrambled to get safely to third.

The Mets connected for a double play to shut the Rangers down in the bottom of the eighth. After Seager struck out swinging, Burger grounded to Lindor at short, who tossed to Semien at second for the second out. Semien then turned to Brett Baty at first to close the half inning.

Brandon Nimmo was stifled at the plate in his final appearance against his former team, walking and striking out once apiece.

In three at-bats, Jung notched three hits, including his first-inning two-RBI home run.

The Mets head to Washington, D.C., for a three-game series against the Nationals to close the regular season, beginning Friday.

LHP Andrew Alvarez (2-6, 3.17 ERA) will take the mound for the home team. New York has yet to name a starter.

articles.title: DR Congo and Ivory Coast top Africa Cup of Nations qualifying opening wins
articles.summary: DR Congo beat Equatorial Guinea, while Ivory Coast cruise by Ghana and Cameroon beat Comoros as AFCON qualifiers begin.
articles.body:
The Democratic Republic of the Congo followed up their World Cup exploits ⁠with a 2-0 ⁠home win over Equatorial Guinea on the opening day of the group qualifiers for next year’s Africa Cup of Nations.

Captain Chancel ⁠Mbemba headed home the opening goal in the fourth minute, and Yoane Wissa added a second 18 minutes from time in Kinshasa on Thursday, although ⁠the scoreline might have been more emphatic after they twice struck the woodwork and also had two efforts ruled offside.

It was the first game for the Congolese after advancing through the first phase of the World Cup for the first time ‌and running England close in their last-32 tie in Atlanta in July.

However, there was no opportunity for home supporters to celebrate their achievement as the size of the crowd at the Stade des Martyrs was restricted to 20,000 after sanctions for fan violence that followed defeat by Senegal in World Cup qualification one year ago.

Mauritania and Namibia were also winners ⁠in Thursday’s early games, while Libya netted a last-gasp penalty ⁠to salvage a 2-2 draw at home to Botswana behind closed doors in Tripoli, where the stadium was also banned because of previous supporter violence.

Botswana striker Tumisang Orebonye scored a double ⁠in the first half to put his side on course for a rare away win before Maruwan Alhibeeshi thrashed ⁠home from the edge of the area to ⁠pull one back in the 87th minute.

Botswana substitute Mothusi Cooper gave away a stoppage-time penalty with a clumsy challenge, allowing Ezoo El Mariamy to rescue a draw.

Mauritania won 3-1 over the Central ‌African Republic in Casablanca, Morocco, which included a superb chipped effort over the goalkeeper from Dawda Camara, while Bethuel Muzeu scored the only goal as Namibia ‌edged ‌Congo.

Ivory Coast beat Ghana 2-0 in a derby in Bouake in a Group C encounter.

A stunning strike from Malick Yalcouye opened the scoring from outside the box in the first half, although the Ghana keeper, Lawrence Ati-Zigi, will feel he should have done better at his near post.

Franck Kessie gave the Black Stars stopper no chance as he sent his opponent the wrong way with a side-footed second-half penalty.

Ghana, who failed to qualify for the 2025 edition of AFCON, are left to reflect on a match where they failed to register a shot on target until the 75th minute. They also conceded 61 percent of possession to their hosts.

Cameroon beat Comoros 3-1, while Tunisia were held to a 1-1 draw by Uganda in the pick of the other ties.

articles.title: Wyndham Clark on Thursday crowds at Medinah: 'Kind of dead out there'
articles.summary: The crowds, if not sparser than expected, were certainly muted for the first session of the 16th Presidents Cup, which the U.S. emerged from with a 3-2 lead...
articles.body:
The Cubs and White Sox both officially clinched playoff berths on Thursday, the former doing so in an afternoon game at Wrigley. Little of that buzz, however, reverberated 25 miles away at Medinah Country Club.

The crowds, if not sparser than expected, were certainly muted for the first session of the 16th Presidents Cup, which the U.S. emerged from with a 3-2 lead.

"It was kind of dead out there," Wyndham Clark said, unprompted. "I felt like the momentum could have been better, to be honest, because we weren't really feeling the fans, I think, as much as normal."

Clark pointed to a shot Morikawa hit on the par-4 11th hole – a 5-wood from 229 yards to 12 feet – and how it drew no applause from the crowd.

"We didn't even know if it was on the green because no one clapped," Clark said. "It was a little surprising. We'd make some big putts…"

Clark then stopped himself before adding, "I'm saying this more as a challenge that hopefully tomorrow and the weekend the fans are out there really rooting us on, and regardless of what happens, we have the momentum."

U.S. captain Brandt Snedeker was later asked about Clark's comments. The American skipper agreed and provided a possible explanation.

"It was a weird day," Snedeker said. "I really felt like the fans were out there and they were there, but the first tee was loud, and then it just kind of dissipated as the day went on. I don't know why. I think part of it was because the golf course was set up pretty difficult. There were some really tough pins out there, so it was really hard to get a lot of birdies going and get guys going crazy, I guess. And there's some tough viewing out there on some of the holes where people really couldn't see what was going on.

"I know what Chicago is built of. I know what kind of fans we've got here. They'll come out tomorrow. We've just got to go out and play good golf."

articles.title: Seahawks' Sam Darnold hopes to return from glute injury and play against the Commanders
articles.summary: Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold is taking his recovery from a glute injury day by day, but said Thursday he hopes to return for Sunday's game at Was...
articles.body:
Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold is taking his recovery from a glute injury day by day, but said Thursday he hopes to return for Sunday's game at Washington.

Darnold practiced Wednesday for the first time since he was injured on the first series of the Seahawks' season-opening win over New England .

"Feeling good," Darnold told reporters Thursday. "For me, especially during this week, taking it day by day. Continuing to balance the reps and do everything I need to get ready."

Coach Mike Macdonald said a day earlier that Darnold had returned to practice but was not taking all of the first-team snaps. He said the Seahawks could determine by Friday whether to start Darnold or backup Drew Lock against the Commanders.

Darnold was hopeful he'd be ready in time.

The plan is for Darnold to gradually increase his practice reps each day. He also has to get in the mindset of "not worrying about the hip at all. Just going out there, playing football, playing fast."

Lock took over in the opener and helped the Seahawks to a 13-10 victory over the Patriots . He started last Sunday's 31-7 win at Arizona .

Darnold did not miss a game last season as he led the Seahawks to a Super Bowl title. He threw for 4,048 yards with 25 touchdowns and 14 interceptions as Seattle won a franchise-record 14 regular-season games.

He admittedly was worried after he was sacked by New England's Dre'Mont Jones in the opener. Darnold sought treatment on the sidelines before limping to the locker room.

"There's some things that happen on the field. You get banged up a bit. Something feels weird and you feel weird coming off to the sideline and you're able to shake it off after a couple of minutes. It wasn't that way. The pain lingered and I wasn't able to throw. That was the main concern," he said.

Darnold was taken to a hospital, where he watched the final minutes of the game on his phone, concerned about how long he'd be out. At first, it was believed that Darnold had a hip injury, but an MRI later ruled that out.

"It had a huge impact of potentially being out for the year to, 'OK, it might only be a few weeks or a couple of weeks.' That changes your mindset drastically," he said. "It was a good boost that I needed while I was in there."

The Seahawks have been just fine so far with Lock, who has thrown four touchdown passes — all to star receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba .

"(Lock) is a baller," Darnold said. "Went out there, played well. Happy for him and it was cool. Cool to see his process throughout the week and how he attacked it. To go out there and perform the way that he did it was no surprise."

articles.title: Another Update On Penta Vs Roman Reigns Rematch
articles.summary: There’s another update on the Penta vs Roman Reigns rematch. For those who don’t know, Roman Reigns defended the World Heavyweight Championship against Penta...
articles.body:
There's another update on the Penta vs Roman Reigns rematch.

For those who don't know, Roman Reigns defended the World Heavyweight Championship against Penta on Monday Night Raw in Mexico City. The match took place on the September 14 edition of the show, where Reigns retained.

Initially, Fightful Select said that a rematch between these two stars isn't expected. But now, things might have changed.

On the latest edition of WrestleVotes Radio on Fightful Select , it was said that many people in WWE creative believe a rematch between Penta and Reigns makes sense.

"Many in creative viewed Penta vs. Roman Reigns as a one-and-done, but that may have changed. Several in creative now believe a rematch makes sense, both from a business & creative standpoint."

The report doesn't say that a rematch is definitely going to happen in the future, but it's still an update. Penta vs Reigns was a success for WWE and Netflix, with the show averaging 3.1 million viewers – the highest after this year's Raw after WrestleMania.

Roman Reigns Will Defend His Title Against LA Knight Next

For now, Roman Reigns is scheduled to defend his World Heavyweight Championship against LA Knight at Money in the Bank. Knight has been a fan favorite for many years now, so a lot of fans want him to win this match.

After Money in the Bank, WWE could revisit a rematch with Penta if they wanted to. Penta is going to be participating in the Men's Money in the Bank ladder match. If he wins the briefcase that night, he could decide to cash it in against Reigns.

articles.title: Detroit SportsNet preseason streaming outage angers Red Wings fans
articles.summary: Fans attempting to watch the Detroit Red Wings’ preseason game via MLB.tv Thursday got about 13 minutes of action before it got stuck in commercials.
articles.body:
A few hours after a Detroit SportsNet social media post exhorting Detroit Red Wings fans to watch the team's third preseason game on Thursday, Sept. 24, or take a penalty , it looks like the nascent team broadcaster will land in the box itself.

Fans attempting to watch the Red Wings ' game at Little Caesars Arena vs. the Buffalo Sabres via the MLB.tv website – the first test of the Wings' streamer after the first two preseason games were shown on DetroitRedWings.com – got about 13 minutes of game action Thursday before the broadcast went to commercial … and never came back.

After about two minutes of commercials, the broadcast devolved into the "COMMERCIAL BROADCAST IN PROGRESS" screen with no sound. That lasted for several minutes, leaving Wings fans unable to watch the first goal of the game, a power play score by Axel Sandin Pellikka. About a minute after that, though, the MLB.tv/DSN broadcast began to carry the audio track from play-by-play announcer Ken Daniels and analyst Mickey Redmond, at least through the end of the period … when the commercials began again.

articles.title: Bills' Josh Allen, Joe Brady reveal biggest challenges Chargers pose
articles.summary: Bills duo Josh Allen and Joe Brady explain what makes the Chargers a tough matchup ahead of Week 3.
articles.body:
The Chargers will face one of the league's best teams this Sunday: the Bills .

Los Angeles will have its hands full against the Bills , as Buffalo looks like a juggernaut and an early favorite to hoist the Lombardi Trophy this season.

As for the Chargers , they look like quite the opposite. They entered the season with much promise; however, after two weeks, many are writing them off.

The Bills are heavy home favorites in the matchup; nonetheless, quarterback Josh Allen is not taking them lightly.

Allen said he's not fooled by the 0-2 start and stated that the Chargers defense has real talent led by Khalil Mack and Derwin James Jr.

"I think that they've got some real talent, Allen said .

"Khalil Mack one of best pass rushers of last 20 years. Still plays at high level. DBs are savvy. Derwin James not afraid to lay the boom."

Head coach Joe Brady praised the Chargers' offense and Mike McDaniel. He said McDaniel challenges opposing defenses like no other.

"You have to defend every blade of grass on the field," Brady said .

"He makes your defense communicate at a high level. They do a good job making things look the exact same."

While Allen and Brady praised the Chargers on both sides of the ball, the reality is Los Angeles hasn't looked sharp on either side.

The Chargers' defense has shown early in the season that it can't consistently cover receivers, especially over the middle, and can't put pressure on the quarterback.

The offense has been sloppy and inconsistent. Whether it's the complex scheme McDaniel has implemented or mental errors, it's been a tough watch, and the offense has managed only 28 points in two games.

The Bills will be the Chargers' toughest challenge yet in what will be their first road game of the season.

articles.title: Why Tyler Reddick Will Be a Contender at Kansas Speedway
articles.summary: Tyler Reddick returns to Kansas Speedway, the site of his latest win in the NASCAR Cup Series.
articles.body:
It was a historic start to the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series season for Tyler Reddick. The driver of the No. 45 kicked off the campaign by winning the season-opening Daytona 500, passing Chase Elliott on the final stretch to become a victor of "The Great American Race."

Reddick backed it up the following week with a win at EchoPark Speedway, becoming the first driver since Matt Kenseth in 2009 to win the first two races of the season. One week later at Circuit of The Americas, Reddick made history by becoming the first driver to win the first three races of the season.

Reddick's winning ways would not stop there as he scored a victory in the Goodyear 400 at Darlington three races later. Then, the 23XI Racing driver passed Kyle Larson on the last lap at Kansas for his fifth victory of the season in just nine races.

Reddick became the first driver since Dale Earnhardt in 1987 to win five of the first nine races of the Cup Series season. However, Reddick has not made it back to victory lane since.

Reddick enters Kansas in a different position compared to April

At one point, Reddick had a 100-plus points lead after his early-season dominance. However, some misfortunes allowed Denny Hamlin, co-owner of 23XI Racing, to close in by the midpoint of the season and take over the top spot.

Hamlin would win the regular season championship and claim the top spot in the Chase, while Reddick's slump had him shuffled back to the third seed when the Chase began three races ago.

After the April Kansas race, Reddick looked unstoppable and was the clear favorite to win the 2026 championship. Now, as the Cup Series gets set to return to Kansas Speedway this Sunday, Reddick finds himself seventh in the points standings, 61 points behind leader Kyle Larson.

Reddick showed promise in the Chase opener with a third-place finish. However, a 25th-place result at World Wide Technology Raceway followed by an 18th-place finish at Bristol has mired Reddick back in the Chase standings.

Why Kansas can be the turnaround Reddick needs

Sunday's Hollywood Casino 400 at Kansas Speedway could be where Reddick turns things around.

For one, Reddick is the defending Kansas winner after starting on the pole and finishing third in both stages. Reddick is a two-time Kansas winner with his other victory coming in the 2023 Hollywood Casino 400.

In his last seven Kansas starts, Reddick has recorded two wins and four top-10 finishes. The 30-year-old has proven speed in qualifying, too, with five top-five starts and a pole in the last seven Kansas races.

With Kansas on the horizon, as well as two 1.5-mile tracks to follow, Reddick could easily turn his title hopes around on Sunday.

articles.title: ABC13 Athlete of the Week: Randle HS running back is a rare talent racking up yards and records
articles.summary: Randle High School running back Landen Williams-Callis might go down as the best running back to come out of the Houston area. ABC13's Joe Gleason caught up...
articles.body:
When Dr. Thomas E. Randle High School senior running back Landen Williams-Callis is on the field, he can't help but stand out.

"I'm an all-around back," Williams-Callis said. "I can juke, use my speed, stiff-arm, run you over with the power I got."

He's a quiet leader that doesn't say much.

"He says what needs to be said," Randle HS head coach Brian Randle said. "He's not going to get up there and do some long speech, win one for the Gipper or anything like that. He's going to say ya'll follow me and we're going to roll, and that's pretty much what we do."

Since Williams-Callis started as a freshman, the Lions are 45-3.

"It's not okay to lose," he said. "You always want to go win and be the best in anything you do."

Besides winning, one of the things Williams-Callis has been really good at is scoring touchdowns.

"I look at the defense before the play and then after that shot, I just go, whatever happens, happens," he said.

Last year, he set the single-season Houston-area touchdown record with 61.

"Do you have a favorite touchdown out of all of them?" ABC13 sports producer Joe Gleason asked.

"Yeah, all of them," Williams-Callis responded.

Last week, he broke the Houston-area career touchdown record.

His cousin, Jacquizz Rodgers , of Lamar Consolidated had held the record of 136 touchdowns since 2007.

Williams-Callis has worked closely with his cousin to improve his game. Often getting advice when the game is over.

"Just coaching me and training me on anything I do wrong," he said. "After every game he'll tell me what I did wrong, and I can use that knowledge to take it to the field or the next practice and work on it."

Landen's sights are set on the next record. With over 8,100 career rushing yards, he needs a little over 3,000 more to become the state's all-time leading rusher.

"He loves to win, and he loves the game of football," Coach Randle said. "It's been a joy to watch."

articles.title: Joe Flacco Makes Feelings Clear on Giants Trade Buzz After Jaxson Dart's Season-Ending Injury
articles.summary: Joe Flacco, the Cincinnati Bengals quarterback, suddenly found his name linked to the New York Giants after Jaxson Dart, the Giants’ starting quarterback, su...
articles.body:
Joe Flacco , the Cincinnati Bengals quarterback, suddenly found his name linked to the New York Giants after Jaxson Dart , the Giants' starting quarterback, suffered a knee injury that will keep him out for the rest of the 2026 regular season. The speculation also carried an obvious connection because Giants head coach John Harbaugh coached Flacco for 11 seasons in Baltimore .

Speaking with Cincinnati Enquirer Bengals beat reporter Kelsey Conway on Thursday, Flacco addressed the speculation directly and made it clear that he does not believe anything involving a move to New York is actually happening.

"I just get a kick out of it," Flacco said during the interview . "I mean, because the stuff happened yesterday, but it's obviously not real and not true. But it was good enough to get people, like certain friends of mine and things like that, to get them to text me, 'Hey, I'll see you in New York.' And I was like, 'No, guys, you won't; you know that's not true.' I kind of just get a little bit of a kick out of it. I haven't really given it too much thought at this point."

The Giants have confirmed that Dart will miss the remainder of the regular season, with Jameis Winston taking over as the starter. Harbaugh has also acknowledged that New York is keeping its options open, including the possibility of adding another quarterback through a trade. That immediately put Flacco into the social-media rumor cycle.

The rumors gained traction because Flacco is currently behind Joe Burrow in Cincinnati. The Bengals acquired him from the Cleveland Browns last year after Burrow's injury, and Flacco eventually returned to Cincinnati on a new deal for the 2026 season. He backed up Burrow during the time he was away dealing with a turf toe.

Flacco and Harbaugh also have plenty of history. Baltimore hired Harbaugh in 2008, the same year the Ravens drafted Flacco, and the two spent more than a decade together. In that time, the duo was able to bring home a Super Bowl victory, with Flacco also winning Super Bowl MVP honors.

The veteran quarterback, aged 41, also visited the Giants last year when he became a free agent, but signed with the Cleveland Browns before eventually being traded to the Cincinnati Bengals . Still, Flacco stressed that his attention remains with Cincinnati rather than the speculation surrounding New York.

"It's not up to me. I'm on the Cincinnati Bengals, and because of that, that's my focus, is just being here, and doing the things I need to do to get better each day while I'm here. … I'm a Cincinnati Bengal and I'm doing everything I can to get ready for the Pittsburgh Steelers ."

Flacco also acknowledged that trades can happen without much warning. He was traded from Cleveland to Cincinnati last season and said he had no idea that move was coming. However, it was a troubling time for him at Cleveland, having gone 1-3 as a starter in 2025.

But when Conway asked whether he had any reason to believe another trade was coming, his answer was straightforward:

Flacco is not the only name being floated around. CBS Sports has also linked the Giants to Tyler Huntley , Justin Fields , Mitchell Trubisky , and Anthony Richardson, while Mac Jones and J.J. McCarthy have emerged as other possibilities. With Harbaugh leaving every avenue open, New York still has several paths to fill the gap.

The Chicago Cubs had one heck of a day on Thursday. Crow-Armstrong spoke to reporters after the game about reaching the impressive feat, via Jesse Rogers of ESPN.

"Recently here I've really felt how badly people wanted it for me. I wanted it, I wanted to put myself in same conversations as such impressive and great players," Crow-Armstrong said. "… You know, it's like if I take the right base it was gonna help the team… I'm so lucky for that realization, that approach to the game. I was just overcome with a lot of different emotions, pretty grateful."

Crow-Armstrong unquestionably helped his team this season. He entered Thursday's game with a 9.8 WAR (wins above replacement) which leads the league , per Baseball Reference. The 24-year-old now has 45 home runs and 40 stolen bases to go along with a .948 OPS, 119 runs scored and 119 RBI.

PHILADELPHIA (AP) — Philadelphia Phillies second baseman Luis Arraez left Thursday's game against Milwaukee with a sprained left ankle after he tried to avoid a tag at first base.

Arraez is a three-time batting champion and entered the game batting .311 to lead to the National League.

Arraez hit a grounder to shortstop Cooper Pratt, and a wide throw pulled first baseman Jake Bauers off the bag.

Arraez dived to his right to avoid the tag and immediately grabbed his ankle. Arraez, obtained from San Francisco at the trade deadline , stayed down for a while as trainers tended to him. He eventually hobbled off the field with assistance.

He left with the game tied 1-1 in the sixth inning. The Phillies needed to beat the Brewers and have the San Diego Padres lose to the Los Angeles Dodgers later in the night to clinch their fifth straight playoff appearance.

Bryson Stott moved from third base to second and Edmundo Sosa took over at third.

articles.title: 3 Reasons to Watch the Cardinals’ Final Series
articles.summary: For the fourth straight season, the St. Louis Cardinals will not make the playoffs. For the third time in those four seasons, they will have a losing record....
articles.body:
For the fourth straight season, the St. Louis Cardinals will not make the playoffs. For the third time in those four seasons, they will have a losing record. While the team has made major progress this season, it is still disappointing given the organization's rich tradition of winning. As a result, it's easy for members of Cardinal Nation to change the channel for this weekend's final series against the Milwaukee Brewers . After all, college football and the NFL have started. The NHL and the St. Louis Blues begin next week.

However, there are three reasons to watch the Cardinals this weekend.

Three Reasons to Watch the Cardinals' Final Series

Two All-Stars have had rough second-half stretches. Jordan Walker , who won the Home Run Derby , has just six home runs since. Riley O'Brien , the team's All-Star closer, has just 14 saves since then.

Despite the rough patches, both enter the Cardinals' final series with a chance to reach some special marks. For Walker, he is two home runs shy of 30 for the season. His 2026 season will not be viewed differently if he doesn't reach that mark. After all, he has over 100 RBI. However, reaching the 30-home-run mark would be a nice exclamation point to his special season. It would also mean he ends the season on a high note after struggling down the stretch.

O'Brien needs two saves this weekend to reach 40 for the season. Reaching 40 saves would put him in the top ten in team history for saves in a single season. Like Walker, O'Brien's season won't be viewed any differently if he doesn't reach the mark, but it would be a nice accomplishment as the team heads into the offseason. Furthermore, he has an outside chance to finish the season as the league leader in saves.

As the Cardinals' final series gets underway, there is no denying the theme of the season has been the youth movement. JJ Wetherholt , Quinn Mathews , and Joshua Baez have all provided memorable moments to give Cardinal Nation hope for the future. Leo Bernal has done the same and is doing so in historic fashion .

Bernal made his debut on September 1st. In 81 at-bats, he is hitting .296 with four home runs and 18 RBI. His 12 RBI in his first ten games set a team record for most RBI in a rookie's first ten games . His 17 RBI in 18 games breaks a team record previously set by Tom Alston in 1954.

When Mark McGwire hit his 69th and 70th home run on the final day of the 1998 season, broadcaster Jack Buck famously asked, "How much more can give us, Big Mac?" That question should be posed to Bernal as the Cardinals' final series begins. How much can he give us in the final three days of his historic first month?

O'Brien is not the only Cardinal with a chance to end the season atop the league in a category. Unlike O'Brien, however, Alec Burleson holds the top spot heading into the weekend. At the time of writing this (Thursday evening), Burleson leads the MLB with 113 RBI, three ahead of Pete Alonso and Sal Stewart .

We have to go back to 2010 to find the last time a Cardinal led the National League in RBI: Albert Pujols . We have to go back even further to find the last Cardinal to lead the entire MLB- Joe Torre in 1971.

Needless to say, Burleson has a chance to make some rare Cardinals' history this season. Given all the great hitters and run producers in MLB, it would say a lot if Burleson can end the season atop the list.

No, the Cardinals are not headed to the postseason or even playing for a winning record. However, there are still reasons to watch the team take the field this weekend.

"He's a work-in-progress. He, like a lot of guys on our team, we lost him for a majority of his rookie year, and certainly a crucial period of time in the playoffs last year. Even a big portion of the regular season," Presti said. "I think he has less game experience than he has NBA experience, if that makes sense. So, every opportunity he has to play, he's going to improve and get better. I just think he has the potential to be a solid defender, in addition to being a dynamic offensive player."

Before the team traveled to Boston , Cox and Mense talked about implementing a wider base with no stride. When Cox tried it out in the cage, Mense recalled him three straight line drives up the middle.

Cox introduced his refurbished mechanics on Aug. 23 and saw immediate results.

From August 23rd to September 16th, Cox slashed .329/.386/.461 in 23 games (86 PA) with 3 homers, a double, and 9 stolen bases. Three weeks of me going gaga here in my mom's basement. Earlier in the piece, hitting coach Hunter Mense put my it plainly: "Anybody that has the kind of toolset that he does is incredibly exciting to watch because you don't know what the ceiling is going to be."

Sometimes, there's added hype from the context. But that's just not the case here. I don't care that the Giants got him from the A's. For Ross Stripling . During Farhan Zaidi's tenure. But that he also flourished under the new player development program run by Randy Winn. It only matters that he's here and he's got me excited about a team I have been invited (and taken the opportunity) to hate a little bit.

But maybe the streak is over. Maybe it's time to take off the rose colored glasses. Maybe it's logical to tone down my excitement. This past week, he's struck out 12 times in 25 plate appearances (48 K%) and is 2-for-20 (.100). That speed and defense has certainly helped prop up his profile overall (he's about a 1 WAR player right now no matter the WAR system), but he's got a lot of swing and miss. Too much. On the season, it's 60 strikeouts to 10 walks in 157 plate appearances. Putting aside the 6:1 ratio, that's still 38.3% overall.

In the minors, it's a far more palatable 23.4% for his career and 17% here in 2026. He hit .400 in the minors this season, you know. It's so easy to root for him and dream big right now. But check out this list of 2B/OF types who had 200 PA or fewer, 15 or fewer walks and 60 or more strikeouts (which I've gone ahead and sorted by rWAR):

I didn't expect to get just 33 results; but, as I suspected, it's not promising. On the other hand — wow, Jonah Cox is the best of this bunch. What I'm looking to see is whether or not this could be a part of a players' track record long-term. To do that, I needed to sort by age. The younger the player, the better chance of this being a sort of rough start to a career.

Players for whom this was their final season

Players who'd play in just 1 more season

Bill Hall (14 MLB PAs for Baltimore ), Gregory Polanco (382 PA for PIT; 72 OPS+), Jhonkensy Noel (153 PA for CLE; 31 OPS+), Trayvon Robinson (164 PA for SEA; 76 OPS)

Drew Stubbs (last game: 5/5/2017 w/Giants), Jake Marisnick (last game: 7/18/2023), Reggie Taylor (2005), Travis Demeritte (2022)

Andrew Knapp (last game: 8/28/2024 w/Giants), Jake Cave (2024), Cory Snider (1994), Chris Owings (2023), Deven Marrero (2022), Mikie Mahtook (2019), Garrett Hampson (2025), JaCoby Jones (2021), Keston Hiura (2025), Brett Phillips (2023)

Egyptian Healy (1885-1892)*, Gorman Thomas (1973-1986)

So, after reviewing MLB history, the most accurate thing we could say is that nothing is set in stone. Cox could go either way. Makes sense. This is his age-24 season. He's got a heckuva MiLB track record. Egyptian Healy (1886) and Gorman Thomas (1973) are the two outliers in this comparison group — Healy was a pitcher who amassed that hitting line — who are from such wildly different eras that a comparison doesn't seem relevant. Just eyeballing the list, if Cox is to have longevity at all, it'll be because of his speed and defense. But will his bat push him into being a regular or is he bound for the bench?

Strikeout rates are as instructive as walk rates — at least, to me they are. There's some research to suggest that Double-A numbers are also strong predictors of MLB success/failure , and so when I mash those two ideas together in my brain I get the idea that Jonah Cox is still making the adjustment to major league pitching. But that 17% MiLB strikeout rate sis a swing and a drive away from the 38.2% he has in his first 157 plate appearances. The scant Statcast data isn't exciting either. 5.8% barrel rate. Just a .213 expected batting average. A 32.7% chase rate.

Still, he's kind of unique. If you filter the age to 24 or younger and set a minimum threshold for stolen bases of 10, then the only comp is that Leody Taveras season, who was graded as one of the best prospects and athletes when he signed as an international amateur in 2015 and as he got older was graded for playing plus defense at a premium position . Now, some speedsters can thrive if they can square up the ball , but Cox isn't at that point — not yet, anyway.

The position comparison doesn't necessarily suggest that regular starter I'd so hoped for either, but he has certainly demonstrated an intensity and physical talent to keep an eye on; the team isn't necessarily set at the position, but at the very least with Gilbert there, too, they've got options in center that they didn't have a year ago.

But, I guess, pump the brakes. Take a breath. Cox is not quite the surprise breakout of this rebuild season, but he has certainly made us all anxious to see if he can take the next step.

articles.title: Vikings' Kyler Murray is grateful he's back from his concussion without much time lost
articles.summary: Kyler Murray could hardly believe his bad luck, forced out of his first game with the Minnesota Vikings after just 11 snaps when he tried to end a run with a...
articles.body:
EAGAN, Minn. (AP) — Kyler Murray could hardly believe his bad luck, forced out of his first game with the Minnesota Vikings after just 11 snaps when he tried to end a run with a slide only to sustain a blow to the side of his head.

His first pass, an ill-advised heave into double coverage after a protection breakdown, had been intercepted.

"You couldn't draw it up any worse, probably," Murray said. "I just felt like I didn't even get to get in the game."

Fortunately for the Vikings, he bounced back quickly. Murray didn't clear the concussion protocol in time to play last week at Chicago , but he'll be on the field on Sunday at Tampa Bay .

"I'm blessed. I'm healthy. I'm excited about not only this week," Murray said, "but the future."

Thanks to backup Carson Wentz and the brilliance of the Vikings' defense , Murray is returning to an undefeated team.

"As a competitor I wanted to play last week, but I understand what the protocol is and how everything shakes out," Murray said after practice on Thursday in his first public remarks since the injury. "I'm thankful that we're 2-0. Shoutout to Carson, coming in and doing a great job. I couldn't be happier for him and this team."

Coach Kevin O'Connell said he thought Murray stood to benefit from watching Wentz play such a steady game without trying to force throws that weren't there, making a point to mention that Murray's interception in the opener came after an unacceptably poor decision.

"We haven't turned it over since. My expectation is we're going to protect the football and play our role offensively while continuing to grow and look like the offense we know that we can become," O'Connell said.

Murray said the only other concussion he's had in his career came in 2015, late in his freshman year at Texas A&M when he tried to slide at the end of a run against Auburn.

"I played the next week," said Murray, who transferred to Oklahoma and won the Heisman Trophy in 2018. "Times were different."

Murray wasn't upset at the Packers defenders who brought him down. Lukas Van Ness grabbed him from behind and Javon Bullard lowered his shoulder to Murray's helmet as he ducked down.

"You chart it to the game. I don't judge anybody over there for anything that happened," Murray said. "We play a violent, dangerous game, and that's just part of it."

Jones makes progress, but the Vikings might need a new punter this week

Running back Aaron Jones (knee) took part in practice on a limited basis on Thursday, a promising sign for Murray and the offense with Jordan Mason (thumb) out for at least three more games. Backup Deejay Dallas (toe) did limited work on Wednesday and Thursday.

Rookie punter Brett Thorson, however, has not practiced this week after straining his hamstring in the rain last week at Chicago. The Vikings signed 15-year veteran Johnny Hekker to the practice squad so they can elevate him as needed.

Thorson beat out Hekker, a four-time Pro Bowl pick, in training camp. Hekker thus gives the Vikings confidence that not only the punting would be fine but the holding operation for kicker Will Reichard would be a smooth transition if Thorson is inactive.

"That's part of the decision obviously of anybody you bring in," O'Connell said. "It's not just about the punt. It's about Will and making sure we don't end up having a two-part process where we're needing to find consistency because Will's been fantastic."

The offense will also have Jauan Jennings back after he missed the last game for personal reasons. He's an experienced wide receiver behind Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison and one of the team's best run blockers.

articles.title: Seahawks will continue right guard rotation with Anthony Bradford out
articles.summary: With Anthony Bradford on IR, Beau Stephens and Christian Haynes will split time at RG against the Commanders.
articles.body:
Seattle Seahawks starting right guard Anthony Bradford was a (kind of) surprising scratch last week against the Arizona Cardinals after picking up a hip injury in practice. Christian Haynes started at right guard in his place, but he wasn't the only one seeing time on the line as rookie Beau Stephens got some snaps as well.

This week, Bradford was placed in injured reserve and will miss at least the next four games. Offensive coordinator Brian Fleury confirmed that Haynes and Stephens will rotate at RG again this week on the road against the Washington Commanders .

"Yeah, I think that those two will continue to rotate in a similar situation. It'll just be determined by the state of the game," Fleury said in Thursday's press conference.

Considering the fact that the Seahawks rushed for over 150 yards against the Cardinals on the way to putting 31 points on the scoreboard, both of those players acquitted themselves well. Fleury agreed with that sentiment, and was pleased by their performance.

"I thought Beau handled his first actual NFL snaps pretty well," Fleury said. "We were deliberate in how we were going to sub him in. It wasn't a set rotation. We just knew that there were going to be times in the game where we could just say, 'Hey, this is going to be your series and see how he functioned, and I thought he did well. I was happy with how Christian played as well with the amount of snaps that he had. That's quite a bit of volume compared to what he's normally gotten."

It remains to be seen whether this rotation will continue for the entirety of Bradford's absence or if either Haynes or Stephens will take hold of the position. Ideally, it would be Stephens since he's under contract for multiple years, but in reality it will almost surely be Bradford's job when he comes off IR. Still, this is a good chance for Haynes and Stephens to try and secure themselves a spot on the burgeoning Seahawks offensive line.

articles.title: Michigan vs Iowa Prediction: Odds, expert picks, team and player news, betting trends, and stats
articles.summary: Iowa Hawkeyes at Michigan Wolverines Game Preview
articles.body:
There's always a battle or some bruising going on in the Big Ten, but rarely are there games where the physicality in the trenches alone will determine the winner. That's what we have when the #17 Iowa Hawkeyes go to the Big House to face #18 Michigan . Both teams are 3-0 and in must-win situations if they want to make either the Big Ten Championship or the College Football Playoff. The game total is 38.5! That's the lowest game total of the entire weekend and for good reason.

Iowa will go to Michigan this weekend then host Ohio State next weekend. After that, Iowa has a bunch of games that are winnable and most of them will list the Hawkeyes as the favorites, but it'll be 12-round boxing match making it out of the regular season with two or fewer losses. Iowa has dominant two out of three opponents, shutting out Northern Illinois (40-0) and Northern Iowa (55-0) in their latest game. In between those two shutouts, Iowa beat rival Iowa State, 16-13 in the usual defensive-minded contest. I don't see that changing here as Iowa has the 107th-ranked passing attack per PFF and Michigan isn't any better at 113th!

Bryce Underwood and this Michigan offense has skated by with below average performances against two really good defense — Western Michigan and Oklahoma , but this could be even tougher. Iowa has always has giants in the trenches and Michigan is no different, but they've failed to find much success on the ground, ranking 131st in rushing success per PFF. Like Iowa, the bread and butter of this Michigan team is the defense. The Wolverines have allowed 39 total points in three games, rank top 25 in rushing defense and 30th in fewest plays for opponents (Iowa ranks 11th).

Let's dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us.

Game Details and How to Watch Michigan vs Iowa

The latest odds as of Thursday courtesy of DraftKings :

Moneyline: Michigan Wolverines (-218), Iowa Hawkeyes (+180)

Head Coach: Kyle Whittingham 2026 Record: 3-0 (0-0) Offensive Points Per Game: 27.3 (62nd) Defensive Points Per Game: 13.0 (T-16th) 2026 Strength of Schedule: 62nd 2026 Remaining Strength of Schedule: 17th

The Michigan offense has been the most disappointing unit for the Wolverines this season. The running game has been the backbone of any success they've had. Michigan ranks 66th in rushing yards per game (147.7) compared to 102nd in passing yards per game (175.7). Bryce Underwood has struggled so much that PFF ranks the Wolverines passing attack 113th in the country — and that's after they whooped UTEP and Underwood tossed two scores.

Michigan Player to Watch on Offense: QB Bryce Underwood

Bryce Underwood definitely had a fire lit after Week 1's postgame presser following his Hail Mary toss over Western Michigan. Hearing that his job isn't infinite, well he turned around and beat #11 Oklahoma then throttled UTEP. Despite his start being shaky against Oklahoma, 9-of-17 for 111 yards, he bounced back against UTEP, as you'd hope. Underwood went 19-of-25 for 223 yards and two touchdowns against UTEP. This will be another challenge and it could be a long day against an Iowa team with eight sacks and three interceptions.

The Michigan defense is holding their opponents to 220.0 yards per game, ranking 10th-best in the country. The Wolverines have held Western Michigan, Oklahoma, and UTEP to 150, 289, and 221 total yards. Michigan has 10 sacks and two interceptions on the early season. The Wolverines haven't faced a threading passing attack yet and won't versus Iowa, so I'd expect Michigan to stack the box and sell out against the run. Michigan has allowed 96.3 rushing yards per game, ranking 23rd.

Michigan Player to Watch on Defense: DE John Henry Daley

John Henry Daley has been a wrecking ball over the last two weeks. He has 2.5 sacks and 11 combined tackles against Oklahoma and UTEP. Last year as an Utah Ute, he posted 11.5 sacks, 48 tackles, and two forced fumbles. His stock is rising and I wouldn't be shocked if he ends up being a first round pick next year.

The Hawkeyes passing attack ranks 107th per PFF, so neither Michigan nor Iowa have a top-100 passing attack. However, Iowa ranks fifth in rushing offense and sixth in run blocking, so you can bet that Kamari Moulton and this Hawkeyes offensive line will be hard at work on Saturday. Iowa had an offensive explosion last week in a 55-0 win versus FCS Northern Iowa. Iowa recorded 645 total yards and 422 on the ground and posted 507 total yards and 289 rushing versus Northern Illinois. Against Iowa State though, the only P4 opponent Iowa has faced, the Hawkeyes yardage dropped to 284, only 13 first downs gained, and 93 rushing yards.

Iowa Player to Watch on Offense: RB Kamari Moulton

It sort of feels like another average Iowa year where this team has problems with the quarterback and the running game is what keeps this offense afloat. Kamari Moulton is that guy carrying Iowa. Moulton had 183 yards and two touchdowns against Northern Illinois, then 57 rushing yards and 31 receiving yards versus Iowa State. Moulton is listed as day-to-day after missing the Northern Iowa game. If he is out, I am not sure how the Iowa offense survives.

In three games, Iowa's defense has allowed 13 total points — all of them coming from Iowa State. The Hawkeyes shut out Northern Illinois and Northern Iowa, which makes sense given those teams are a combined 1-5 with a lone win over Drake . Iowa has yet to allow a first quarter or fourth quarter point this season. The defense will carry the Hawkeyes as far as they can, but this is a must-win if Iowa wants to make the College Football Playoff or Big Ten Championship Game.

Iowa Player to Watch on Defense: LB Cam Buffington

Cam Buffington has an eye-popping 27 tackles through three games as a full-time starter. The next highest tackler on the team has 10, so he's lightyears ahead at this point. Against Iowa State, Buffington had 15 tackles with nine of them being solo, which again, the next closest player on the team has 10 tackles in three games and he had 9 solo in one game. With Michigan's inability to have explosive plays, I would say another double-digit tackling performance may be on the docket for number 33.

"When Iowa and Michigan meet on Saturday, the game total will be the lowest of the week by a full touchdown. In Iowa's only P4 game against Iowa State, the score was 16-13. In Michigan's only P4 game, the score was 17-10 versus Oklahoma. This feels like first to 20 points wins. I am not a believer in either quarterback situation at either school and the rush defenses are so strong that Jordan Marshall and Kamari Moulton could struggle. articles.title: 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa misses practice with calf, knee concerns
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers pass rusher Nick Bosa, who has had three torn ACLs, missed a second straight practice, indicating his leg issues may be a cause for conce...
articles.body:
Four San Francisco 49ers veterans rested during Wednesday's practice: defensive end Nick Bosa , running back Christian McCaffrey , offensive tackle Trent Williams and linebacker Dre Greenlaw . Of those four, Bosa was the lone player who did not return to the practice field Thursday in Santa Clara.

On Wednesday's official practice participation report, the 49ers listed Bosa status as: "Not injury related - resting player, Knee." Of course, the 28-year-old tore his right ACL last season. It's normal for a player with his injury history - Bosa has suffered three torn ACLs during his football career - to sit out the first practice of the week. The 49ers gave him the same treatment last week in the leadup to their Week 2 matchup with the Miami Dolphins .

Here's where things get strange. Bosa returned to the field last Thursday in a limited capacity. He was a full participant Friday. This time around, he was absent again on Thursday, and San Francisco handed down a new injury designation: "Knee, Calf."

Bosa, who typically speaks to reporters on Wednesdays during the regular season, was not made available in the locker room. Nor was he on Thursday.

The extent of Bosa's calf injury is currently unclear. As is the status of his knee.

Despite clearly working his way back into game shape, Bosa has been an impactful player. Among 49ers defensive linemen, he ranks second in pressures (six), trailing only defensive tackle Osa Odighizuwa , according to SūmerSports. Bosa's five pressures during Week 2 led the team, and his 69 snaps through two weeks lead San Francisco's edge rusher room.

Bosa's injury isn't the only one to monitor. Wide receiver Mike Evans (hip) did not participate for the second consecutive day on Thursday. Evans did work off to the side during the portion of practice open to the media, running routes without pads.

articles.title: 'We didn’t eat, drink or sleep': Rowers Satnam and Salman recall turmoil before historic Asian Games bronze
articles.summary: NAGOYA: Earlier this week, Typhoon Dujuan disrupted the Asian Games schedule and triggered a storm of a different kind in Indian rowing.
articles.body: NAGOYA: Earlier this week, Typhoon Dujuan disrupted the Asian Games schedule and triggered a storm of a different kind in Indian rowing.A contingent that won five medals at the previous edition in Hangzhou will return home with just one — a bronze won by Satnam Singh and Salman Khan in the men’s double sculls.The duo had originally been entered in the quadruple sculls before being moved to the doubles following 11th-hour changes by the Rowing Federation of India (RFI), which attributed the reshuffle to the curtailed competition schedule.At the Nagaragawa International Regatta Course in Gifu Prefecture on Thursday, Satnam and Salman stayed in the leading pack for much of the race. China’s Xudi Yi and Yide Nie eventually pulled away to win gold in 6:09.77, ahead of Uzbekistan’s Mekhrojbek Mamatkulov and Pavel Sorin (6:10.49). The Indian pair finished in 6:13.25.The medal dulled the bitterness of the previous few days, but did little to erase it.“The hardest part was that we were removed from the quadruple and placed into the doubles. We were depressed. We didn’t eat or drink or sleep that night. We were harassed and had no recovery,” Salman said.With a medal at stake, a first for India in the Asian Games men’s double sculls, the rowers had to put the upheaval aside.“The next day, we woke up and felt that what matters most is the country and the flag. We have to keep it high. Whatever happens later will happen. We want to make sure that whatever happened to us shouldn’t happen to any other rower,” Salman said.“We had a chance to raise the flag of our country high but we lost it. Koi nahi. Jo kismat mein hota wahi milta hai. If it is in our destiny to win something, then it is impossible to stop it,” he added.Satnam, though, could not help wondering what might have been.“The situation we faced two days before was very unexpected. If we had been formed four months ago, then we could have been fighting for gold,” said the Navy rower. “But I am feeling proud since we have never won a medal in double sculls. I feel sad for my partners (from the quadruple sculls) because a good medal has gone from our hands.”Upset by the changes before the race, Salman recalled the advice his coaches gave him before the race: “Salman, aisa chappu maro ki nadi ka paani bahar aa jaye. articles.title: Juanjo Gutiérrez: "Es muy probable que Galán y Lebrón jueguen juntos”
articles.standfirst: El seleccionador español atiende a MARCA tras anunciar la lista de 8 convocados para el Mundial de pádel 2026
articles.summary: El seleccionador español atiende a MARCA tras anunciar la lista de 8 convocados para el Mundial de pádel 2026
articles.body: Juanjo Gutiérrez (Málaga, 1982) es el seleccionador de España desde hace ya más de un lustro. El mismo que logró la histórica victoria del 2021, el mismo que cayó en 2022 y 2024 en el tercer punto. Un técnico con carácter que, guste o no, no rehúye la presión, muere con sus ideas y que ha compuesto una selección “agresiva” para el Mundial. Gutiérrez atiende a MARCA Pádel apenas minutos después de haberse hecho oficial una lista que se ha llevado con hermetismo hasta su oficialización y que ha confirmado lo que este periódico adelantó el pasado mes de mayo, que Aimar Goñi era el gran tapado. ‘El Bisonte’, junto a Jon Sanz, ha sido el último nombre que ha dado por cerrada una lista donde Coello, Galán, Lebrón, Nieto, Yanguas y Navarro eran fijos. El seleccionador aborda con este periódico la convocatoria, una más que hipotética final ante Argentina, si volverá a probar con Lebrón y Galán para definir la serie o su adiós en caso de no conseguir traer el título mundialista a España. P: ¿La primera pregunta es obvia: por qué esta lista de convocados? R: Me he basado en en un patrón de juego agresivo, en un patrón que genere muchos winners y donde también habrá errores no forzados porque jugando en Doha el error no forzado es más habitual que en una pista indoor, pero apostado por una selección con autoridad y muy valiente. P: La gran novedad en esa selección es Aimar Goñi del que hemos hablado mucho en Marca porque sabíamos que entraba en tus planes. Es un jugador en plena formación, podríamos decir, pero que precisamente encaja en ese patrón de juego agresivo del que nos estás hablando. ¿Por qué Aimar? R: Porque para mí combina un poco lo que considero que se va a demandar más en esas condiciones, que es mucha valentía, mucho winner. Tiene un gran carácter competitivo y a mí encima me ha me ha asegurado que con la selección más y él tiene ya experiencia en la etapa de menores. Le llevo viendo desde desde hace muchos meses y creo que es un jugador que va encajar muy bien en el equipo y que va a rendir mucho. P: Siempre has comentado que tenías unos seis fijos y que variaba una plaza por cada una de las posiciones. La otra novedad, podríamos decir, aunque no lo es, es la incorporación de Jon Sanz en esa cuarta posición del drive.... R: Jon también tiene un juego muy frontal y también consigue conectar muchos winner, Por supuesto también errores no forzados, pero ya te digo que en esas condiciones lo soporta la pista. Pero tiene una cosa muy buena también y es que ha jugado con todos los reveses, cierto. Y ha rendido muy bien con ellos…, así que considero que un jugador tan polivalente como John a nivel de combinarlo con diferentes jugadores puede ser clave. P: ¿Es España mejor? ¿Es favorita? La realidad es que las últimas dos ediciones del Mundial por selecciones ha perdido en el tercer partido. ¿Cómo ve el seleccionador esta participación por parte de España? R: Como dicen varios jugadores que son muy sabios, que son muy veteranos, el dato mata el relato. Hoy Argentina es mejor que España. P: ¿Es mejor o es favorita? Por eso esa doble pregunta. R: Para mí es mejor. Por datos. Hablando de mundiales, evidentemente. Los últimos años ha cambiado bastante el panorama, pero para mí sigue siendo siendo mejor o, como mucho, te compro que sea muy igualado. Pero yo no veo a España favorita como tal, para mí es una selección que tiene un potencial brutal y que por suerte tenemos jugadores que por nivel, podrían haber estado en este equipo y haber venido a jugar si llega a ser en otro país el evento. Hay un gran trabajo detrás de muchísima gente y tenemos un fondo de armario de jugadores excepcional. P: De ese fondo de armario y por las condiciones del evento que va a ser en outdoor, se han quedado fuera de la lista nombres como Fran Guerrero, Javi Leal, Momo González o Edu Alonso. ¿Has hablado con los no convocados? R: La prelista podía haber sido de 16, pero lamentablemente tenía solo 12. He hablado con ellos y evidentemente pues se muestran un poco contrariados, tristes. Es normal, es lógico, pero sinceramente, por nivel tienen para estar en este equipo. Pero solamente puedo llevar ocho y bueno, considero que son los jugadores idóneos para esta cita. P: De esos ocho, dando por sentado que evidentemente España y Argentina son las potencias hegemónicas en el pádel y las que a priori, si todo se da bajo la lógica deportiva, se encontrarán en la final, saldrán los seis que compondrán una hipotética final a tres puntos. ¿Juanjo Gutiérrez tiene ya más o menos dibujada en su cabeza la alineación? R: Sí, la tengo. Pero primero hay que dejar pasar estas semanas que también hay competiciones, porque hay que ver cómo llegan, a qué punto de rendimiento llegan al torneo y después allí siempre entrenamos y hacemos pruebas para ver cómo combinan, juegan o se sienten. Ten en cuenta este deporte que es tan bueno que es un deporte tan sensitivo, tan sensorial y tan, tan de estados de ánimo. P: Probablemente en la última edición del Mundial la gran apuesta del seleccionador fue volver a unir en pista a Juan Lebrón y Alejandro Galán, ex pareja número uno del mundo, y que desde que habían dejado de ser compañeros no habían vuelto a jugar en un torneo. Es una pregunta que está en el ambiente del pádel…, ¿existe la posibilidad de que vuelvan a jugar juntos con con España? R: Sí. Sí, sí, por supuesto. P: Es algo que que has hablado con ellos previamente o que dentro del espíritu de equipo, de selección. es más propicio que se dé como la última vez… R; No lo he comentado, pero yo creo que ellos lo entienden y lo deben saber en su interior porque están jugando por España, por su país y la selección está por encima de de jugadores e individuales. Entiendo que yo creo que sí que lo saben y que no creo que haya ningún problema. Pero sí, sí, es muy probable que jueguen. P: ¿Imagináis cuál puede ser la convocatoria de Argentina? Todos damos por hecho que por momento de carrera y rendimiento va a haber también novedades y que nombres como Sanyo Gutiérrez, Tello, Maxi Arce, Gonza están ahí. R: Bueno, Argentina tiene jugadores que están haciendo una gran mitad de temporada y los veo a todos muy en forma. Evidentemente ellos son una raza que compite con la selección de forma diferente, que compiten muy bien. Si llegamos a la final, que así debería de ser, va a ser muy duro. Yo si los veo bastante bien. Y sí que tenemos evidentemente ciertas ideas, pero es que pensar en lo que hacen ellos y a lo mejor dejar de pensar en lo que tenemos que hacer nosotros, resta energía. P: La última pregunta viene a raíz de unas declaraciones que creo que te escuchamos en el torneo de Buenos Aires donde decías que si España no ganaba este Mundial, Juanjo Gutiérrez presentaba su su dimisión. R: Yo creo que cuando se tienen objetivos de este tipo, de este nivel, si no se consiguen en un cierto tiempo hay que dar un paso al lado y quizás hace falta que se prueben otras cosas para para buscar el éxito. Aparte, esto es un objetivo deportivo y vital para muchos de nosotros. Para muchos hablo dentro del equipo, jugadores, cuerpo técnico…, cuando ya hay una etapa de varios mundiales que no se consigue, pues a lo mejor hay que dar un paso al lado y hay que ser consciente de ello. P: La pregunta era al revés, ¿si España gana el Mundial habrá Juanjo Gutiérrez en 2028? R: Por mí sí, pero no depende de mí. La decisión la toman otros.

articles.title: Toyota integrará 400.000 robots en sus fábricas y pedirá a los trabajadores humanos que los entrenen: les prometen que no le sustituirán
articles.standfirst: La compañía japonesa busca la convivencia entre estos sistemas y las personas
articles.summary: La compañía japonesa busca la convivencia entre estos sistemas y las personas
articles.body: Toyota planea desplegar 400.000 robots en sus fábricas de todo el mundo a partir de 2028, con una inversión estimada de 1 billón de yenes anuales (unos 6.400 millones de dólares). La estrategia de la multinacional japonesa contempla que estos sistemas convivan y colaboren con las personas, prometiendo que su objetivo es complementar la fuerza laboral humana y no reemplazarla. Del total de las máquinas, unas 150.000 unidades se destinarán a las plantas propias de Toyota Motor y las otras 250.000 se integrarán en empresas filiales y proveedores del grupo como Denso y Aisin. Hiroki Nakajima, vicepresidente ejecutivo del grupo, señala que ve un mundo “donde los robots coexistirán con los humanos, en lugar de reemplazarlos”. Gracias a la inteligencia artificial corporizada, los robots humanoides (como el prototipo ELEY), podrán aprender tareas complejas directamente observando los movimientos de los maestros artesanos humanos a través de cámaras y sensores, eliminando la necesidad de programar software avanzado. La empresa argumenta que esta tecnología busca mitigar la acuciante escasez de mano de obra y el envejecimiento poblacional que sufre Japón, delegando los trabajos más pesados, repetitivos o peligrosos a las máquinas para que los empleados asuman roles de mayor valor técnico y supervisión. De hecho, los directivos aseguran que en el futuro, los robots que hayan aprendido también servirán para entrenar a los nuevos empleados humanos. A diferencia de la estrategia de Toyota, enfocada en un diseño híbrido con ruedas y de desarrollo mayoritariamente interno, sus principales competidores (como Tesla o BMW) han optado por formas puramente antropomórficas y se dividen entre el desarrollo vertical propio o las alianzas con startups tecnológicas. Ahora, la competencia ya se mide en cuántas horas consecutivas puede un robot sostener el ritmo de una línea de producción real.

articles.title: Who is Suruchi Singh? 19-year-old with 5 World Cup golds in one season goes from 26th in 10m air pistol individuals to Asian Games gold in mixed
articles.summary: Suruchi Singh and Kamaljeet won the maiden gold medal in shooting for India at the Asian Games 2026 after a stunning performance in the mixed team event.
articles.body: Suruchi Singh and Kamaljeet won the maiden gold medal in shooting for India at the Asian Games 2026 after a stunning performance in the mixed team event.Kamaljeet and Suruchi shot a total of 484.6 in the final. They were followed by South Korea’s Suhyeon Hong and Gaeun Choo, who finished second with 478.0. The Korean pair were 6.6 points behind Kamaljeet and Suruchi, underlining the Indian duo’s dominance in the final.Iran bagged the bronze medal with 415.8.But Suruchi’s journey to the Asian Games gold medal was far from easy. The 19-year-old comes from a humble family in Haryana, and when TimesofIndia.com spoke to her coach Suresh Singh last year, he recalled how he agreed to train her, but only after laying down his own conditions.From Jhajjar’s fields to the shooting rangeBorn in Jhajjar, Haryana, Suruchi comes from a humble family. Her coach, Suresh Singh, has previously recalled how the youngster remains closely connected to her roots, helping with work at home and even operating farm machinery.“If she weren’t at the World Cup today, she’d be home harvesting wheat,” Suresh had told TOI.When Suruchi and her father, Inder Singh, first met the coach, her father made his priority clear: he wanted his daughter to learn discipline alongside the sport. Suresh agreed to take her on, but with a condition, Suruchi would have to follow his system rather than simply focus on pulling the trigger.That decision changed her career.Suruchi won medals at the 2022 and 2023 Nationals before producing a spectacular breakthrough in 2024, when she won seven gold medals at the National Championships in Delhi. She followed that up with two more gold medals at the National Games in Uttarakhand.In 2025, Suruchi began making headlines on the ISSF World Cup circuit, winning individual gold medals in Lima, Buenos Aires and Munich.The ritual before every big matchDespite her international success, Suruchi has retained one habit that keeps her connected to the person who helped shape her career. Before a competition, she calls her coach. Even at major international events, she would contact Suresh minutes before stepping onto the range.“Sir, I have five minutes before I go in, what should I do?” she would ask.The Asian Games gold also reflected the mentality Suruchi has developed through years of training. If she decides to fire 150 shots during a training session and the final shot does not land where she wants it to, Suruchi does not simply pack up and leave. She keeps shooting until she gets the result she wants.Asian Games gold completes another breakthroughThe road to Friday’s gold had not been entirely smooth. Suruchi finished 26th in the women’s individual 10m air pistol qualification at the Asian Games, while India also missed out on a medal in the women’s team event.But the mixed team event offered another opportunity.Suruchi and Kamaljeet seized it. They topped the qualification before carrying that momentum into the final. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India’s shooters missed out on a medal in the men’s 50m rifle 3 positions individual event at the Asian Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya on Friday,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s shooters missed out on a medal in the men’s 50m rifle 3 positions individual event at the Asian Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya on Friday, despite securing silver in the team competition earlier in the day. Asian record holder Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar finished fifth in the individual final, while Niraj Kumar came last among the eight finalists, bringing a disappointing end to India’s campaign in the event.Aishwary, who had qualified third for the final, managed 327.6 points to finish fifth. Niraj, who had entered the final in fourth place in qualification, could only score 299 points to finish eighth.China’s Liu Yukun claimed gold with 360.5 points, setting a new Asian Games record. His compatriot Zhang Changhong took silver with 360.2 points, while Kazakhstan’s Islam Satpayev secured bronze with 348.3 points.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleAishwary and Niraj fail to convert qualification form into medalsThe result was a setback for India after both shooters had shown promise in the qualification round. Aishwary, the Asian record holder, had finished third, while Niraj secured the fourth qualifying spot. However, neither could maintain that position in the final as China swept the top two places.The individual event disappointment followed India’s silver-medal finish in the men’s 50m rifle 3 positions team competition. Aishwary, Niraj and Rudrankksh Patil combined for a score of 1762-94x, finishing just behind China, who secured gold with 1766-95x. South Korea took bronze with 1751-87x.Aishwary scored 589-34x to finish third in the team qualification standings, while Niraj recorded 588-34x to place fourth. Rudrankksh, with 585-26x, finished ninth and missed out on a place in the individual final.India had won gold in the team event at the 2022 Asian Games but surrendered their title to China in Aichi-Nagoya.India’s shooting tally reaches 10 medalsIndia’s shooting contingent has now collected 10 medals at the 2026 Asian Games, including one gold, five silver and four bronze medals. The only shooting gold so far came on Friday, when Suruchi and Kamaljeet won the 10m mixed air pistol event.The Indian pair defeated South Korea 484.6 to 478.0 in the final, with Iran taking bronze on 415.8 points. India’s winning score also broke the Asian record of 481.3, previously set by Uzbekistan at the Asian Shooting Championships in New Delhi earlier this year.India’s overall medal tally at the Games stood at 19 on Friday, comprising two gold, eight silver and nine bronze medals. The women’s cricket team had earlier secured India’s other gold, defeating Sri Lanka by 147 runs in the final.The rifle team silver added to India’s medal haul, but the failure to convert two strong qualification performances into an individual podium finish left the shooters without another medal in the event.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
