articles.title: Brennan Oliver powers Jay to victory over South San in District 14-5A-I opener
articles.summary: The running back rushed for nearly 200 yards with a pair of touchdowns, and the Mustangs defense shined in the victory over the Bobcats.
articles.body:
Brennan Oliver ran for two touchdowns in leading Jay to its first win of the season in a 26-13 victory over South San Thursday in the District 14-5A-I opener at Gustafson Stadium.

Oliver rushed for 197 yards, including big scoring runs of 56 and 80 yards, as Jay (1-3, 1-0) successfully opened its defense of the district crown it won last season.

Jay overcame sloppy play with Oliver's big night and an opportunistic defense, which forced and recovered three fumbles and took advantage of a few special teams miscues from the Bobcats. The Mustangs won despite being outgained by South San (2-1-1, 0-1) in total yardage, 293 to 275.

Jay coach Joshua Campbell earned his first career win with the victory. Campbell is in his first season as the Mustangs' head coach, coming from Sotomayor where he was the defensive coordinator last season.

After starting the season with losses to three Class 6A programs, Campbell said he and the coaching staff worked on and tried to correct a few things during their bye last week.

"It feels amazing," Campbell said on earning his first career win. "Our team got humbled. We were playing very competitive 6A teams. Hats off to Warren, Madison and Roosevelt. It was back to the drawing board, and our bye week came at a critical moment. We practiced hard. We focused on attention to detail. And we just regrouped and told the guys to focus on the process and keep chipping away, and good things were going to happen, and it was evident tonight."

Oliver, a junior, said the Jay players are learning to trust their new coach and his system.

"We started working on our passing game and perfecting our running game and just trusting each other," Oliver said. "We just had to start trusting in him (Campbell), and we know he has a plan for us. So, we just have to follow that."

Campbell said Oliver delivered for Jay when they needed him the most.

"I mean, we rely on our run game," Campbell said. "We needed that type of night from Brennan Oliver. He's certainly a special talent and he's a fantastic young man and the offense goes through him. He showed out tonight, and it was evident in our win."

Jay got off to the fast start as Oliver dashed around the left side for a 56-yard score on the third play of the game, putting the Mustangs up 7-0 at the 10:39 mark of the first quarter.

"I figured out they (South San) couldn't contain the outside, that's where I thrive," Oliver said about his scoring runs. "So, I just kept on taking advantage of that."

South San came up with a big play on its ensuing possession, as Owls quarterback Jacob Sepeda connected with his brother, Joshua Sepeda, on a 49-yard pass play to the Jay 15-yard line, setting up an Octavio Castillo 26-yard field goal that made the score 7-3.

After holding Jay to a three-and-out, South San took its only lead of the game, 10-7, on a 5-yard scoring run by Romeo Suarez on fourth-and-goal with 2:57 left in the first quarter.

Jay regained the lead early in the second quarter on quarterback Drew Skelton's 3-yard scoring run, set up when Jordan Contreras blocked a South San punt and returned the loose ball to the Owls 2-yard line.

The Mustangs had numerous opportunities to expand their 13-10 lead before halftime but had two touchdowns negated on penalties and had a field goal attempt blocked.

After halftime, Suarez provided South San a spark when he returned the second-half kickoff 61 yards to the Jay 25. A personal foul penalty against Jay put the Owls at the Mustangs' 11. But that gain was negated by a holding penalty, and South San had to settle for a Castillo 36-yard field goal, which tied the score at 13 with 8:50 left in the third quarter.

Later in the third quarter, South San was marching toward the Jay goal line when Mustangs linebacker De Antaye King recovered an Owl fumble. Three plays later, Oliver made South San pay for the mistake when he went inside and then cut to the outside on his way to an 80-yard touchdown run early in the fourth quarter to put Jay back in front 20-13.

After a bad snap forced a 15-yard loss for South San on the ensuing possession, the Owls had no choice but to punt. The Mustangs took advantage of the good field position as Skelton scored his second touchdown of the game on a 9-yard run with 5:07 remaining.

articles.body:
Rob Gronkowski has spent years catching touchdown passes from Tom Brady . Now, the former New England Patriots tight end is apparently ready to help his longtime quarterback with his dating life.

While appearing on "TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle," Gronkowski found himself answering an unexpected question about the type of woman who might be a good match for his longtime friend Tom Brady.

Sheinelle Jones quickly stepped in and suggested that Brady simply needs someone who is "kind."

Gronkowski agreed but took the answer a step further. "Sweet, got a great soul, very positive energy… Someone like my mother, she's very sweet," Gronkowski said. "Not my mom, but someone like my mom! She would be like that's the best birthday present ever!"

The comment brought plenty of laughs, but it also highlighted the playful relationship the two former teammates have maintained long after their playing careers.

Brady and Gronk's Friendship Goes Way Back

Brady and Gronkowski built one of the NFL's most productive quarterback-tight end connections during their time together.

articles.title: Glasnow delivers strong final tune-up despite Dodgers loss
articles.summary: LOS ANGELES — Tyler Glasnow walked off the mound Thursday night having done almost everything the Dodgers could have asked of him.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES — Tyler Glasnow walked off the mound Thursday night having done almost everything the Dodgers could have asked of him.

The result, however, belonged to the Padres.

Glasnow carried a no-hit bid into the sixth inning and struck out 11 over 6⅓ innings in his final tune-up before the postseason, but the Padres broke through late and held on to beat the Dodgers, 4-2, in the final home game of the 2026 regular season at Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium.

The Dodgers finished the night 97-62, having already secured a first-round bye earlier Thursday. The Padres, meanwhile, clinched a postseason berth and will play in a Wild Card Series.

And with the postseason bracket beginning to take shape, there is a very real possibility these two teams could be back here in nine days.

For six innings, though, Glasnow looked every bit like a pitcher the Dodgers will want leading their rotation into October.

Ethan Salas broke up the no-hitter with a one-out single in the sixth. Salas eventually scored on a sacrifice fly, and two more singles helped the Padres add to its lead.

Glasnow entered the inning with the Dodgers still searching for their first run. He left it with the Padres ahead.

His final line was as sharp as the circumstances allowed: 6⅓ innings, three hits, three runs, all earned, two walks and 11 strikeouts on 91 pitches, 58 for strikes.

"I feel like I'm in a pretty good rhythm right now, so it's perfect time to bring it in to the postseason," Glasnow said afterward.

The 11 strikeouts came on 79 pitches before he returned for the seventh, and the outing offered another encouraging sign for a Dodgers rotation preparing for the most important games of the season.

The Dodgers had opportunities against the Padres but repeatedly failed to capitalize, stranding seven runners through the middle innings.

Mookie Betts , meanwhile, continued to do what he has done all season: reach base.

Betts reached safely in all four plate appearances, going 3-for-4 with a double, two singles and a walk.

Shohei Ohtani also collected two hits, including an RBI double in the ninth inning that brought the Dodgers within two runs. Ohtani's late hit gave the Dodgers one final spark, but the Padres closed the door to finish off the regular-season home finale.

Dave Roberts said he has liked what he has seen from Ohtani over the past two games.

"The last 2 nights, he's looked great," Roberts said.

The Dodgers' final home game also provided another encouraging glimpse of Edwin Díaz .

Díaz worked a scoreless ninth, allowing no hits and striking out two on just 11 pitches. Since returning from the injured list, he has thrown four scoreless innings, allowing one hit and one walk while striking out eight.

Over his last four appearances, opponents are 1-for-13 with eight strikeouts.

Díaz said his slider is in its best shape right now, a development that comes at an important time as he tries to earn a spot on the Dodgers' postseason roster.

"I'm trying just to do my job. I'm just gonna wanna put zeros when they give me the ball," Díaz said. "I'm ready to pitch every day. I just want them to keep trusting me and keep giving me the ball just to show them I'm ready to pitch in the postseason."

Roberts called Thursday Díaz's best performance of his four appearances since returning.

"This has been the best of the four," Roberts said.

There are only three regular-season games remaining, but the Dodgers have already accomplished one of their primary objectives. The first-round bye is secured. The home schedule is finished. Now comes the final push toward October.

The loss also did little to concern Roberts about the Dodgers' record against winning teams during the second half.

"I don't think so, I don't put stock into it," Roberts said. "Once you get to the postseason, it's a different game."

That is the challenge waiting for the Dodgers.

Thursday was less about the standings than it was about getting their pieces in place. Glasnow looked in rhythm. Díaz continued to build momentum. Ohtani looked sharp at the plate. Betts reached base four times.

The Padres, meanwhile, celebrated a postseason berth in the visiting clubhouse.

There is still baseball to be played before October arrives. But with the Dodgers holding a bye and the Padres headed for the Wild Card round, Thursday's matchup may have offered a preview of a game that matters much more.

"We're gonna have an exciting postseason, so just ride with us," Roberts said.

articles.title: Sparks news: Nneka Ogwumike gives emotional speech after final game
articles.summary: There was not a dry eye at Crypto.com Arena on Thursday when Los Angeles Sparks forward Nneka Ogwumike delivered her farewell speech after playing her final...
articles.body:
There was not a dry eye at Crypto.com Arena on Thursday when Los Angeles Sparks forward Nneka Ogwumike delivered her farewell speech after playing her final game in the WNBA .

Unfortunately, they did not get the victory, losing to the Golden State Valkyries by a hair, 76-75. Ogwumike missed a five-footer that would have given the Sparks the lead with 12.4 seconds left in the fourth quarter.

Ogwumike ended her decorated career with 17 points, 15 rebounds, and five assists.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The 36-year-old star, who led the Sparks to the championship in 2016, turned emotional during her postgame speech.

"I wouldn't go down any other way, which is competing hard here in LA against great competition. It's such a privilege and an honor to be in this league, to be a woman in sports, and especially to wear the Sparks jersey," said Ogwumike.

She thanked her family, who were literally behind her on her special evening, and the fans, calling them the "pulse" of the Sparks.

"I'm still thinking about how I wish I could've left you guys with a win, but I do want you to know that I left my heart out here on the floor, and I'm really happy that I got to share a lot of this with my teammates. You guys really helped me through this season," said the former MVP.

To end, Ogwumike issued a plea to everyone, which underscored the selflessness, leadership, and vision that made her one of the all-time greats, including off the court.

"We cannot ignore the needs of the majority for the noise of the minority. So keep supporting the W. Keep supporting the Sparks. Every little thing that you do, it helps women's basketball grow. Don't think that you can't be a part of this because you all are the reason why we are able to stay here, play this game, play our worth, and continue to change history," added Ogwumike.

She finished her 15-year career with averages of 16.8 points, 7.6 rebounds, and 1.5 steals with the Sparks and the Seattle Storm . She was an eight-time All-WNBA, a seven-time All-Defense, an 11-time All-Star, and a four-time winner of the Sportsmanship Award.

Ogwumike was named to the WNBA 25th Anniversary Team in 2021.

articles.title: Lions Get Definitive Answer on Joey Porter Jr. Trade Rumors
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions could be losing an opportunity to land Joey Porter Jr. as the Steelers cornerback said he plans to play in Pittsburgh. The post Lions Get D...
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions are hurting in their secondary after a string of injuries, leading insiders to speculate that they could make a run at Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to fill the void.

But it appears the hope of trading for the star cornerback could be fading.

Porter made a strong statement about his future with the Steelers, which could put to rest the trade rumors that have surrounded him for weeks amid a contract impasse with the team.

Joey Porter Jr. Will Play for the Steelers This Season

Though Porter missed the first two weeks of the season with a back injury, he told reporters on Thursday that he does plan to play this season. Porter also seemed to push aside speculation that he was disgruntled over the failure to reach an agreement on a contract extension.

"It didn't get done," Porter told reporters about the contract extension he was seeking. "It didn't happen. That's really just old news for me now. It's mainly just focusing on what I have ahead of me and getting back to 100 percent."

Porter added that he "definitely" sees himself playing this season, leading several teammates to voice their support during the locker room interview.

As trade rumors around Porter were starting to grow at the beginning of this season, the Lions were identified as a top potential landing spot. Detroit has been hit hard by injuries to their secondary, losing safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph to injuries before the season started and watching defensive back Avonte Maddox suffer a season-ending injury in last week's loss to the Buffalo Bills .

NFL reporter Jason La Canfora suggested that there was no "easy or imminent solution" to the contract impasse, as the Steelers have a policy not to negotiate contract extensions during the season.

The Steelers could grow tired of Porter's distractions and entertain trade offers, La Canfora suggested.

"These aren't your father's Steelers, they aren't wedding to old-school philosophies anymore and we get the strong suspicion that moving this talented player is reaching the 'addition by subtraction' stage of these types of standoffs," La Canfora wrote .

CBS Sports analyst Bryan DeArdo suggested the Lions could take a few avenues to landing Porter, including a trade that would send a first-round draft pick to Pittsburgh. He suggested the Lions could land Porter and a third-round pick in exchange for first- and sixth-round picks.

"Really, this trade should be as simple as the Lions trading a first-round pick to the Steelers for Porter," DeArdo wrote. "Porter's value to Detroit is greater than next year's first-round pick. The Steelers can use that pick to draft another starting-caliber player. It's a win-win for both teams."

articles.title: Hooker Oghre signs contract extension with Bristol
articles.summary: Bristol Bears hooker Gabriel Oghre signs a new contract with the Prem club.
articles.body:
Bristol Bears hooker Gabriel Oghre has signed a new contract with the Prem club.

Oghre has played 63 games for Bristol since his debut in 2023, scoring 26 tries.

The 28-year-old has also been capped once by England against the USA in July 2025.

"Gabs has developed into one of the leading hookers in the Prem," director of rugby Pat Lam told the club website.

"He's been outstanding for us over the past couple of seasons. His athleticism, power and skillset really suit the way we want to play and at 28, Gabs is coming into the prime years of his career.

"The most exciting thing is we believe his best is still to come."

Bristol have not confirmed the length of Oghre's new deal.

Oghre has returned to the squad in time for the start of the 2026-27 Prem campaign, having missed the end of last season after twisting his knee away at Newcastle in April and requiring surgery.

He previously played for Wasps, Leicester and had a spell in France with Bordeaux-Begles before moving to the West Country outfit.

"The way we want to play really suits me and gives me the freedom to express myself," Oghre said.

"While the coaches have continued to challenge me to improve all areas of my game."

articles.title: Merritt Island pulls away from Titusville, Satellite wins Beach Bowl
articles.summary: Merritt Island remained undefeated with a 39-16 win over Titusville while Satellite defeated Cocoa Beach in the Beach Bowl.
articles.body:
In the first meeting since last year's state playoff matchup, Titusville traveled to Merritt Island for a big District 8-3A matchup.

The 4-1 Terriers hung around for a half, but undefeated Merritt Island showed its depth outlasting Titusville in a 39-16 victory.

"I thought we came out good. It was a wet game early on, so it was a little sloppy early on offense. Defensively, we came out on fire," Merritt Island head coach Tyler Murray said. "We had a pick six. Special teams played lights out, so we were flying around on the defensive side of the ball. We held a pretty good team to 16 points."

The Mustangs were jumpstarted by big plays from a pair of transfers in senior Elijah Floyd and sophomore Elijah Mitchell .

After Titusville senior Dewight Jenkins intercepted Merritt Island senior Kevin Verpaele, Floyd intercepted Terriers senior Remy Vigne on the next play and returned it 21 yards for the game's first touchdown.

It was Floyd's first interception as a Mustang. He entered the game second on the team in tackles.

"He's (Floyd) an unbelievable football player. I hope North Dakota State was watching. They were talking to me about him a little bit (today)," Murray said. "I hope they were watching because he's a great player and somebody's going to get lucky with a kid flying underneath the radar."

Mitchell finished the night as Verpaele's top target with 4 receptions for 120 yards and 2 touchdowns. He posted his second 100-yard receiving game of the season.

Mitchell doubled the Merritt Island lead to 14-0, spinning out of tackle and sprinting to the end zone for a 76-yard touchdown. The sophomore scored the final touchdown of the night on a 37-yard reception.

"The win was good. We came out here to play and we just came out here to do good," Mitchell said. "I told my quarterback before the play to throw me the ball and I'll make a play. I caught the ball and he tried to tackle me. All I saw was the end zone."

Mitchell has fit in seamlessly into the Merritt Island offense in his first season. The sophomore leads the team with 510 receiving yards and 5 touchdowns.

"Coach Murray pushed me hard every day and that's really why," Mitchell said. "We're hungry and we want to win."

Titusville scored on the first play of the second half to trim the deficit to four, but Merritt Island snatched the momentum right back on a 99-yard kick return for a touchdown by senior Kamar Fielder. It outscored the Terriers 22-3 beginning with the kick return.

Verpaele rushed for a 12-yard touchdown and finished the night with 246 total yards and 3 touchdowns. The Mustangs put the game away scoring touchdowns on the first three times they touched the ball in the second half.

"We missed a couple early on. We had a couple holding calls that really put us behind the chains," Murray said. "When you do that kind of stuff, it's really tough to dig yourself out of it. Luckily our defense played well and they got the job done for us."

Merritt Island enters the bye week with a 6-0 record. It'll have two weeks to prepare for its district showdown at Eau Gallie on Oct. 9.

"We're really close to where we want to be. We got a really good opponent in two weeks. A really big game, so we're going to get to work and figure out what we got to do to win that game," Murray said. "Us coaches have been working on them for a couple weeks already, so I'm excited to see. It's not a week off. It's an opportunity to get better. That's how we approach it."

Titusville competed with Merritt Island in the first half, recording the game's first takeaway on an interception by Jenkins. It forced a second takeaway in the fourth quarter on a fumble recovery by senior Matthew Graham.

However, the Terriers were unable to convert those takeaways into points.

"I said going into this whoever's defense plays the best will win. Our defense played good for a long time. Hats off to Merritt Island, their coaching staff, their team," Titusville head coach Matt Diesel said. "They got a really good team. They got a ton of size. They got a bunch of athletes. They do a really good job. They brought a good game and we couldn't keep pace there in the end."

Titusville's defense limited Merritt Island's offense to a season-low 283 total yards. The Mustangs entered the game averaging 439.8 yards per game.

However, the special teams struggled in flipping field position. Merritt Island recorded an average starting field position of midfield.

It also allowed a controversial kick return for a touchdown as it appears senior Khamari Fletcher forced a fumble of Fielder at the 3-yard line with the ball rolling out of the end zone for what would have been a touchback. The refs ruled a touchdown on the play.

"That's correction and fix No. 1. Our kicker has an incredible leg. He's been putting the ball in the end zone at a very high percentage and we haven't had to cover a lot of kickoffs," Diesel said. "(Tonight), you seed the wind and all that good stuff and we didn't quite get it into the end zone and we are deficient right now on our kickoff coverage. Our punt coverage was not great. We definitely got some special teams stuff to iron out."

Offensively, it took some time for the Terriers to get into rhythm. Senior quarterback Remy Vigne battled through shoulder tightness and sat out a possession in the second quarter in which Titusville turned to senior Tank Harvey to quarterback the team.

Harvey finished the night with 104 total yards and 1 touchdown. The senior scored on a 32-yard run in the second quarter to make it 14-6, capping a 9-play drive that he quarterbacked in which he rushed the ball 5 times for 54 yards. He also caught 3 passes for 40 yards and played on defense.

"Tank (Harvey) is all dog. He will go until his arms fall off, his legs fall off. He's as good as a football player as I've been around. He's an exceptional kid," Diesel said. "He does a lot of things for us at a really high level. In the screen game, playing defensive back, jet sweeps, he does all kinds of stuff. He can even throw the ball. You can't say enough good things about Tank Harvey."

Vigne improved his play in the second half, throwing an 81-yard touchdown pass to junior Deion Bland on the first play of the second half to cut the deficit to 17-13. The senior ended the night completing 9-of-19 passes for 184 yards, 1 touchdown and 2 interceptions.

"He had some tightness in his shoulder early and couldn't quite get it going. The ball was just off. We know Remy (Vigne) when he's on and we know when he's not quite 100%. Remy's going to give you everything he's got," Diesel said. "He's a great kid. He works his tail off. Nobody cares more than he does, but (tonight) there were times where he just didn't have it to go and then there were times where he looked like he was doing pretty good."

Titusville dropped to 4-2 and it'll host Davenport on Oct. 2. Diesel said he knows where the team needs to go from here heading into the home stretch of the season.

"Merritt Island is certainly right now playing a good brand of football," Diesel said. "For us to come out here and get pushed and compete as well as we did … obviously, we show up to win but for us to compete and be in the game, it will help us out down the stretch finishing out the season."

The Commodores extended their winning streak to three games, picking up their second district win with a home shutout of Astronaut.

Eau Gallie senior Donovan Richardson opened the scoring on a 5-yard touchdown run. Senior Joseph Allen completed his first touchdown pass of the game to junior Tay Johnson for a 19-yard score.

Commodores junior Troy Silberzahn scored a 3-yard touchdown run. Allen threw a 43-yard touchdown to junior Zay Hawkins and a 32-yard touchdown to senior Lukas Viselli.

Eau Gallie enters its bye week with a 4-2 record as it'll host Merritt Island on Oct. 9. Astronaut dropped to 2-3 and it'll host Space Coast on Oct. 2.

In a battle of unbeatens, the Scorpions ran away in the Beach Bowl outscoring the Minutemen 34-6 in the second half to keep hold of the surfboard trophy.

Satellite senior Raiden Kerr rushed for 2 touchdowns. Seniors Anthony Romero, Liam Nolte, Adrian Garcia and Tristan Sejeck scored 1 rushing touchdown. Senior Brody Grennan threw touchdown passes to senior Noah Corriveau and senior Brennan Saxe.

Cocoa Beach ended Satellite's defensive scoreless streak at 260:04 on a touchdown pass by junior Jay Craft to senior Langston Long with 37 seconds left in the first half. Minutemen freshman Jordan Stevens returned a kickoff 64 yards for a touchdown in the second half.

Satellite stings Cocoa Beach in Beach Bowl battle of undefeateds

Satellite improved to 6-0 and it'll head to Eustis on Oct. 2. Cocoa Beach moves to 5-1 and it'll head to Palm Bay on Oct. 2.

articles.title: Patriots news: Josh McDaniels brushes off early struggles with a car analogy
articles.summary: The New England Patriots are searching for offensive rhythm early in the 2026 NFL season, but offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels has no interest in pressin...
articles.body:
The New England Patriots are searching for offensive rhythm early in the 2026 NFL season, but offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels has no interest in pressing the panic button. Despite securing a 20-3 victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers , New England 's attack remains a work in progress.

Rather than making drastic tactical overhauls to fix early hiccups, McDaniels believes in maintaining a steady course. Speaking to reporters on Thursday, the veteran play-caller used a vivid driving metaphor to describe how New England is managing its growing pains. Beat reporter Mark Daniels captured McDaniels' perspective on X.

"The first month of the season is about growth and improvement," McDaniels said. "If you turn the wheel and jerk the car, you're going to have a problem."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

McDaniels' philosophy centers on patience over panic as the unit gels. Starting quarterback Drake Maye showed promise against Pittsburgh, completing 14 of 22 passes for 208 yards and an interception.

Wide receiver Romeo Doubs delivered the explosive play of the game with a 63-yard connection to set up an Andy Borregales field goal, while running back TreVeyon Henderson added punch with a 39-yard touchdown run in his season debut. Still, the defense carried much of the load with a fumble recovery touchdown, leaving Maye to admit the offense needs more spark and consistency moving forward.

McDaniels understands that early-season execution is rarely flawless. With head coach Mike Vrabel building a physical culture, McDaniels wants Maye and the offense to trust the system rather than overcorrecting after every mistake. Making sudden, reactionary adjustments often creates more chaos than solutions.

As New England prepares for its next test, McDaniels remains confident that steady, disciplined driving will steer this young offense in the right direction.

articles.title: Liverpool lining up sensational move to bring back their own Paul Pogba
articles.summary: Liverpool are now looking at signing their very own Paul Pogba and bringing him back to the club. The Reds desperately need to invest in their midfield. Sinc...
articles.body:
Liverpool are now looking at signing their very own Paul Pogba and bringing him back to the club.

The Reds desperately need to invest in their midfield. Since the summer of 2023, when they did sign four midfielders in fairness, they have not brought in further reinforcements in that department.

Even this summer after Curtis Jones departed for pastures new, Liverpool ignored the position deciding to promote the phenomenally talented Trey Nyoni instead.

Nyoni is an excellent midfielder and he does deserve a bigger role in the team. However, he doesn't solve the Reds' issues completely.

Right now, Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch are like opposite magnets, who just don't fit together in a double pivot.

It's why Liverpool need a different profile of a midfielder.

Liverpool's attempts to sign a midfielder

The Reds have long sought to bring in a more defensive minded midfielder.

It started with the pursuit of Aurelien Tchouameni, which failed. That was followed by a double failure when trying to lure Moises Caicedo and Romeo Lavia to Anfield.

And then it was Martin Zubimendi 's turn to reject the advances of the Reds. He decided to stay at Real Sociedad before ultimately joining Arsenal .

This summer Liverpool did explore a move for Lamine Camara , who came close to signing for Chelsea and that would have been another player they missed out on.

But in the end, Camara stayed at Monaco , and he may be a player the Reds will target next year. But he won't be the only one.

Tyler Morton could become Liverpool's own Pogba

According to a report in TEAMtalk , Liverpool are one of the clubs considering a move for the Lyon midfielder in 2027.

The report claims Morton is liked by a number of potential clubs with the Reds being among them.

Obviously, Morton came through the ranks at Liverpool's academy and even made several appearances for the first-team. He was part of the Reds' first-team squad as they won the Premier League under Arne Slot.

Then Morton was sold to Lyon, where he has thrived in Ligue 1 - establishing himself as one of the best young midfielders in the league.

Now, the Reds look like they are lining up a move for him. And in the process they could be signing their very own Pogba, considering Manchester United did the same with the Frenchman. They sold him to Juventus and then brought him back for a lot more money.

articles.title: Santos FC, Monica's Gang unveil Magali line for Mauricio's 90th
articles.summary: Long established in Monica’s Gang stories as a Santos fan, Magali now officially wears the club’s colors. The character stars in a collection launched by San...
articles.body:
Long established in Monica's Gang stories as a Santos fan, Magali now officially wears the club's colors. The character stars in a collection launched by Santos Futebol Clube, MSP Estúdios, and Só Ídolos in honor of Mauricio de Sousa's 90th birthday.

The line includes shirts, caps, cups, cushions, coasters, keychains, and popcorn buckets. The items feature a special version of the character inspired by the club and are aimed at both Santos FC supporters and readers who follow Magali in the comics.

With the concept "From Vila to Brazil," the partnership brings together two stories that were born in the state of São Paulo and went on to win over the whole country. On one side is Santos FC, the club that introduced Pelé to the world and continues its tradition of developing athletes, from the Meninos da Vila to the Sereias da Vila. On the other is Mauricio de Sousa, who turned characters created in comic books into part of Brazilian culture.

The choice of Magali reinforces a connection that already existed. The character has always been identified as a Santos supporter and now comes to represent that passion beyond the stories as well. The collection is part of the celebrations marking Mauricio de Sousa's 90th birthday and celebrates the meeting of two worlds held dearly in the emotional memory of different generations: Monica's Gang and football.

MSP Estúdios, founded by Mauricio de Sousa, is responsible for franchises such as Monica's Gang, Chico Bento, and Horácio. A pioneer in character licensing in Brazil, it has established itself as one of the country's leading names in entertainment, producing comic books, books, animations, films, series, games, music, and a wide range of content that combines creativity, innovation, and original storytelling. Its mission is to entertain, inspire, and promote culture through works that address universal themes, such as the value of friendship, always aligned with a commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion.

With an expanding portfolio and standout projects across multiple platforms, MSP explores new creative frontiers, both by adapting its worlds to contemporary formats and by developing initiatives that connect in a unique way with audiences of all ages. A signatory of the WEPs (Women's Empowerment Principles), a UN Women initiative in partnership with the Global Compact, MSP Estúdios also works alongside UNICEF, WWF-Brazil, and other internationally recognized organizations.

articles.title: Jota’s return a major boost for Celtic but patience is needed
articles.summary: Celtic’s Superstar from Portugal nears his long awaited return but Celtic supporters have to be patient and realistic as ACL injuries are the hardest to come...
articles.body:
Celtic's Superstar from Portugal nears his long awaited return but Celtic supporters have to be patient and realistic as ACL injuries are the hardest to come back from…

Jota of Celtic receives treatment before leaving the field during the ScottishPremiership match between Dundee United and Celtic at Tannadice on April 26, 2025. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

Jota set for contact challenge during the international break, but he shouldn't be rushed into a comeback. A word of caution is perhaps needed too. Celtic supporters need to be realistic about his hopes of a full recovery…

Jota's good news welcome during a time of negativity around Celtic

Some good news during a time of negativity around Celtic at the moment when it was revealed yesterday that long term injury victim Jota is being lined up to take part in a bounce game during the international break.

Jota of Celtic celebrates after scoring his team's second goal during the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Heart of Midlothian at Celtic Park on March 29, 2025. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

The Portuguese winger has been sidelined since April 2025 after suffering an ACL rupture in a 5-0 win over Dundee United at Tannadice, a result that clinched the league title for the Hoops.

Jota has been making significant progress in training

It's understood that Jota has been making significant progress in training, but has yet to be tested in 'contact' football, so the next step is naturally to arrange a bounce game to get the 27 year old fully prepared for a first team comeback.

Jota of Celtic celebrates after scoring his team's second goal during the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Hearts at Celtic Park on March 29, 2025. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

If the fans favourite comes through that challenge unscathed, then a first-team return next month is a distinct possibility.

Martin O'Neill previously predicted a Jota return around Halloween

Martin O'Neill has previously spoken of the players recovery, and was optimistic of his chances of a return by around Halloween but that was the timeframe that the Celtic manager originally suggested a few months ago.

Jota of Celtic acknowledges the fans after the Scottish Cup Quarter-Final match between Celtic and Hibernian at Celtic Park on March 09, 2025. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

However speaking on 7 September, the Celtic boss said via Glasgow Times : "Jota might be ready more quickly than I thought. He's coming along very well. It's been a long time, but he's been doing really well in small-sided matches he's been involved in.

"Jota's not been stretched too much yet but that will come for him over this month."

A return for the former Benfica man would come as a huge boost to the club in light of recent poor results. However, it should be urged as a note of caution that we shouldn't expect the 27 year old to immediately start showing the ability we know he fully possess.

Jota of Celtic celebrates after scoring his team's second goal during the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Dundee United at Celtic Park on February 15, 2025. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

Jota has endured 18 months on he sidelines

18 months is a long time to have been absent the game, and this type of injury could effect his chances of returning as the same player.

We all hope differently of course, but we all need to bear that in mind.

Add to that the fact that Jota had played very little football since leaving Celtic after the June 2023 Scottish Cup Final win over Inverness Caley Thistle to sign for Al-Ittihad where he was seldom played before moving to Rennes where once again first team minutes were limited.

Jota's record at Celtic has been exceptional

Jota contributed 28 goals and 26 assists in 83 games over two years at Celtic playing under Ange Postecoglou. He averaged a goal or assist every 111 minutes, and that's clearly a level that none of the Celtic wingers are close to achieving.

That standard is what the Celtic fans are dreaming of seeing again from Jota. Haste ye back son!

Last weekend we got to hear the Maeda song for one last time now this old favourite could be coming back into the Celtic songbook and what a joy it will be to hear it again and watch Jota on the wing for Celtic…
